notation.meaning: fraction of edges that join a node of class \(i\) (source) to a node of class \(j\) (target); sums to 1. For an undirected graph each edge is counted in both orders, so \(e\) is symmetric
fractions of edge ends at the source and at the target side in class \(i\), respectively \(j\)
values (a node property such as degree) at the source of an edge and at the target of an edge
standard deviations of \(a_i\) and \(b_j\) as distributions over the property values: \(\sigma_a^2=\sum_i a_i x_i^2-(\sum_i a_i x_i)^2\)
trace of \(e\): \(\sum_i e_{ii}\)

formulas.name: Assortativity by a scalar property (Newman 2002, 2003)
formulas.where: Pearson correlation between the values at the two ends of an edge; with \(j,k\) the property values (degree measured as remaining degree in Newman 2002, equivalently the degree itself, since the correlation is shift-invariant). Defined when \(\sigma_a\sigma_b>0\); a regular graph has zero variance, so r is not defined.

formulas.name: Assortativity by a categorical attribute (Newman 2003)
formulas.latex: r=\frac{\sum_i e_{ii}-\sum_i a_i b_i}{1-\sum_i a_i b_i}
formulas.where: Compares the fraction of edges inside a class with the fraction expected if ends were paired at random with the same marginals; 1 for perfect within-class mixing. The denominator is 0 when all edge ends are in one class (\(\sum_i a_i b_i=1\)): not defined. Defined only when there is at least one edge, since the \(e_{ij}\) are fractions of edges.

formulas.name: Directed degree assortativity
formulas.latex: r=\frac{\sum_{jk} jk\,(e_{jk}-a_j b_k)}{\sigma_a\sigma_b}\quad(j=\text{degree at source},\,k=\text{degree at target})
formulas.where: Same formula over the arcs, with the source value taken from one degree type (in or out) and the target value from another, giving the four in/out choices.

formulas.name: Weighted version
formulas.where: Each edge counts with its weight in the mixing fractions (and the degree values are strengths when strength assortativity is scored); weights non-negative and not all 0.

variants.assort: The scalar-property coefficient of Newman 2002 (degree) computed on a generic assortativity entry point (the binary or weighted adjacency matrix in BCT, with direction flags); the formula is the Pearson form above.
variants.assortativity_degree: The Pearson formula with the property fixed to node degree (out-degree at the source, in-degree at the target for directed graphs, or the degree itself for undirected ones), optionally with direction ignored.
variants.assortativity_nominal: The categorical formula: \(r=(\mathrm{Tr}\,e-\sum a_ib_i)/(1-\sum a_ib_i)\) over a vertex partition or attribute, with optional directedness and edge weights.
variants.assortativity_values: The Pearson formula for any numeric vertex property (not only degree), optionally weighted and directed; the correlation is taken over edge ends of the values.

formulas.name: Average nearest-neighbour degree (Pastor-Satorras, Vazquez and Vespignani 2001)

formulas.name: Degree connectivity
formulas.where: Average of the nearest-neighbour degree over all nodes of degree \(k\); an increasing function signals assortative mixing.

formulas.name: Weighted average nearest-neighbour degree (Barrat et al. 2004)
formulas.where: Neighbour degrees weighted by tie weight and divided by the strength; defined for \(s_i>0\).
